title: Three-cell ambient compact-support comparison and refinement equation
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes; their structure maps need not be separated [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On small pro-etale sites choose either $\mathcal D_T=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ at a fixed level, or $\mathcal D_T=D(\mathscr S_T)$, where $\mathscr S_T$ is the category of sheaves of $A_n$-modules $M_n$ with semilinear quotient transitions $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_{n+1}\to A_n}M_n$ and componentwise transition-compatible morphisms. Use the ordinary unbounded, simultaneous ringed-diagram-site operations [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $P_u=Lu^*$, $S_u=Ru_*$, $J_a=a_!$, and use the canonical conjugate compositors $d:P_uP_v\cong P_{vu}$, $c:S_vS_u\cong S_{vu}$, $e:J_bJ_a\cong J_{ba}$ and normalized proper/open mate $\Gamma_Q$ of [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting]. All equations include these compositors and the tensor associators. In the system case they are equations before evaluation or total limit, with every quotient transition retained.
Supply opens $X\xrightarrow l U\xrightarrow a V\xrightarrow b\overline X$, $Y\xrightarrow d W\xrightarrow k\overline Y$, $Z\xrightarrow i\overline Z$, and proper maps $m:U\to Y$, $r:V\to W$, $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$, $q:W\to Z$, $s:\overline Y\to\overline Z$, $t:\overline Z\to T$. Require $ra=dm$, $pb=kr$, $sk=iq$, with these three squares Cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $f=ml$, $g=qd$, $h=ti$ and
$$\mathsf A=\Gamma_{(a,d,m,r)},\quad\mathsf B=\Gamma_{(b,k,r,p)},\quad\mathsf C=\Gamma_{(k,i,q,s)}.$$
For each binary tower define its raw comparison by whiskering its $\Gamma$ with the outside proper and open functors and then applying $c,e$; it is a map between the candidates $F_{(j,u)}=S_uJ_j$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. The two binary-comparison paths for $(h,g,f)$, expanded from $S_tJ_iS_qJ_dS_mJ_l$ to $S_tS_sS_pJ_bJ_aJ_l$, are respectively
$$L=(S_tS_s\mathsf B J_aJ_l)(S_t\mathsf C S_rJ_aJ_l)(S_tJ_iS_q\mathsf A J_l),$$
$$R=(S_tS_s\mathsf B J_aJ_l)(S_tS_sJ_k\mathsf A J_l)(S_t\mathsf C J_dS_mJ_l).$$
They satisfy $L=R$. After the canonical $c,e$ contractions this is exactly equality of the path comparing $(g,f)$ then $(h,gf)$ with the path comparing $(h,g)$ then $(hg,f)$. The equality commutes with the directed comparison maps for every compatible proper refinement of such staircases (maps of all ambient and intermediate schemes commuting with the opens and proper arrows and restricting to identities on $X,Y,Z,T$). No projection map, invertibility of a raw comparison, or geometric existence of a staircase is assumed; only the specified unbounded pro-etale or intrinsic system operations are used.

proof.text: The comparison for $(g,f)$ uses $\mathsf A$, and that for $(h,g)$ uses $\mathsf C$. For $(h,gf)$ the square is the vertical paste of B above C. The vertical equation of [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting] expands its mate as $(S_s\mathsf B)(\mathsf C S_r)$. For $(hg,f)$ the square is the horizontal paste A followed by B; the horizontal equation expands its mate as $(\mathsf B J_a)(J_k\mathsf A)$. Whisker these equations by the indicated outside functors $S_t,J_l$ and insert the binary comparison definitions. They give exactly the displayed words $L$ and $R$ before contraction.

source.place: Tag 0F7K (lemma-pseudo-functor), three-cell grid and final naturality calculation; agent extension using the ambient pasting statements, including proper refinements

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary object $K$ on $X$ and put $x=J_dS_mJ_lK$, $y=S_rJ_aJ_lK$, $u=\mathsf A_{J_lK}:x\to y$. Naturality of $\mathsf C:J_iS_q\to S_sJ_k$ at $u$ says $(S_sJ_k)(u)\circ\mathsf C_x=\mathsf C_y\circ (J_iS_q)(u)$. Applying $S_t$ and postcomposing with $(S_tS_s\mathsf B)_{J_aJ_lK}$ gives $R_K=L_K$. Since natural transformations are equal exactly when all their components are equal, $L=R$. This is the elementary naturality square itself, with no cancellation or invertibility.

source.place: Tag 0F7K (lemma-pseudo-functor), three-cell grid and final naturality calculation; agent extension using the ambient pasting statements, including proper refinements

proof.text: The contractions at the source and target use the same canonical $c,e$. Their associativity and naturality, stated in [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting], identify the two bracketings with the common expanded functors. Composing $L=R$ with these identifications proves the asserted equality of contracted binary-comparison paths. Functor composition and its whiskering involve no tensor input; any tensor associators already present are simply carried along by these natural identifications.

source.place: Tag 0F7K (lemma-pseudo-functor), three-cell grid and final naturality calculation; agent extension using the ambient pasting statements, including proper refinements

proof.text: To check proper refinements explicitly, use primes for one refining binary tower. Write its proper maps of ambient schemes as $v_U:U'\to U$, $v_V:V'\to V$, $v_W:W'\to W$, with $v_Ul'=l$, $v_Va'=av_U$, $v_Wd'=d$, $rv_V=v_Wr'$, $mv_U=m'$ and $qv_W=q'$. Let $D=\Gamma_{(a',a,v_U,v_V)}:J_aS_{v_U}\to S_{v_V}J_{a'}$ and $E=\Gamma_{(d',d,1,v_W)}:J_d\to S_{v_W}J_{d'}$. Let $H_l=\Gamma_{(l',l,1,v_U)}:J_l\to S_{v_U}J_{l'}$ and $H_{al}=\Gamma_{(a'l',al,1,v_V)}:J_{al}\to S_{v_V}J_{a'l'}$. All are defined by [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting], even when the refinement squares are not Cartesian. Its horizontal equation gives $H_{al}=(D J_{l'})(J_aH_l)$, with $e$ inserted. Thus the directed candidate maps are $C_U=S_mH_l$, $C_W=S_qE$, $C_V=S_{qr}H_{al}$, after $c,e$ identify their targets with the primed candidates.

source.place: Tag 0F7K (lemma-pseudo-functor), three-cell grid and final naturality calculation; agent extension using the ambient pasting statements, including proper refinements

proof.text:
There are two vertical factorizations of the square with top $a'$, bottom $d$, left $m'$ and right $rv_V=v_Wr'$. One stacks $(a',a,v_U,v_V)$ above the unprimed square A; the other stacks the primed square A' above $(d',d,1,v_W)$. Both give its intrinsic mate by [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting]. Hence, with the canonical $c$ inserted,
$$(S_rD)(\mathsf A S_{v_U})=(S_{v_W}\mathsf A')(E S_{m'}).$$
Whisker by $J_{l'}$ and precompose with $J_dS_mH_l$. On the left, naturality of $\mathsf A$ at $H_l$ moves $H_l$ across $\mathsf A$, and the horizontal equation of Step 5 combines the resulting $D J_{l'}$ and $J_aH_l$ to $H_{al}$. On the right, naturality of $E$ at $S_mH_l$ moves this morphism across $E$. After applying $S_q$ and contracting, the result is
$$C_V\,\alpha_{g,f}=\alpha'_{g,f}\,(C_W*C_U),$$
where $*$ is the horizontal composite of the two directed candidate maps. This proves the required binary refinement square using only two pasting equations and two naturality squares.

source.place: Tag 0F7K (lemma-pseudo-functor), three-cell grid and final naturality calculation; agent extension using the ambient pasting statements, including proper refinements

proof.text: Apply the binary refinement square of Steps 5-6 to A and to the vertically pasted B+C square. Paste those two squares using naturality of the outer candidate map to obtain the exterior leftPath refinement square with exactly sourceMap and targetMap. The already proved equality leftPath=rightPath for both staircases transports this square to the rightPath square, without a second four-tower calculation. Every calculation uses the same canonical compositors, with their equality transports, and no refinement mate is inverted.

source.place: Tag 0F7K (lemma-pseudo-functor), three-cell grid and final naturality calculation; agent extension using the ambient pasting statements, including proper refinements

proof.text: The ambient theorem [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting] states all the used equations on the entire unbounded pro-etale or intrinsic semilinear-system categories, before evaluation, restriction of scalars or total limit. Steps 2-7 are equations of natural transformations in those categories. They therefore retain all quotient transitions. None takes equality from its evaluations, inverts a raw comparison, uses a projection map, or constructs a staircase: the staircase and its proper refinements were supplied.
